title: NHS jobs and the Health and Care Worker visa: check the role before you apply
summary: A practical guide for international graduates and overseas-trained clinicians. Check professional registration, sponsorship for the vacancy, pay and which visa applies before committing to an offer.
content:
# NHS jobs and the Health and Care Worker visa: check the role before you apply

Last updated: 2026-11-26

## Start with the vacancy
An NHS job does not automatically qualify. The Health and Care Worker visa is part of the Skilled Worker route. You need an eligible job, an approved sponsor and a Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS). An NHS organisation, an eligible NHS supplier or an adult social care provider may sponsor eligible roles. Find the actual vacancy, check the employer’s legal name on the sponsor register and ask recruitment whether the named team sponsors this post. Do not rely on standard wording in an advert. [Employer checks](#guide-evidence-start)

## Check registration separately from the visa
Doctors should check General Medical Council (GMC) registration with a licence to practise and any grade-specific requirement. Overseas graduates may need to take PLAB or qualify through another GMC route. Nurses and midwives should check Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) requirements for qualifications, English evidence and a Test of Competence where applicable. For protected titles such as physiotherapist or radiographer, check the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). Use its international route if you trained overseas and it applies to you. Ask which stage requires registration and what happens if it is delayed. Registration gives no guarantee of employment or sponsorship. [Regulators](#guide-evidence-registration)

## Get the occupation code, salary and hours in writing
Ask recruitment for the duties, SOC occupation code, work location, guaranteed basic pay, contracted weekly hours and pay scale or point if applicable. The usual annual floor for eligible health and care roles is £25,000, with the applicable going rate or national pay scale also to be met. For jobs on national pay scales, check the relevant UK nation and the scale for the role. Compare actual contracted pay and hours against the correct rules. An NHS band alone does not establish eligibility. If you hold Student permission, confirm when you may switch; the course-completion, job-start and doctoral exceptions are separate checks. [Pay and switching](#guide-evidence-vacancy)

## If you do not have a healthcare qualification
Consider roles matching your skills, such as administration, data or laboratory support, while you have permission for that work. Check the duties and professional requirements for each role. A support or administrative post may be outside this visa route; check separately whether it qualifies for ordinary Skilled Worker sponsorship. For example, HCPC registration does not make a physiotherapy assistant vacancy equivalent to a registered physiotherapist post. Ask about sponsorship before counting on the offer. If you are considering adult social care, read the [care worker switching guide](/en/work-visa/adult-social-care-worker-sponsorship). [Role eligibility](#guide-evidence-support)

## Budget for the application and check the family position
The application fee still applies. Eligible applicants and eligible dependants do not pay the Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) on this route. Allow separately for any regulator fees or tests. Check dependant eligibility by occupation; care-worker and some other medium-skilled roles have restrictions. Time in qualifying sponsored permission may count towards the current five-year Skilled Worker settlement route if the other conditions are met. Wider earned settlement reform does not change the criteria unless the relevant rules take effect. Read [switching work visa routes](/en/work-visa/skilled-worker-switch-extend-change-employer) and [Skilled Worker settlement](/en/work-visa/skilled-worker-settlement-ilr). [Fees and family](#guide-evidence-budget)
